summary: Draft updated at submission.json and validated read-only (valid, no diagnostics). With both ReadIndex leads already answered and no execution pending, this turn is a source trace that selects a different A2 direction: how a leader turns a membership proposal that fails propose-time validation into log state. The new investigation @confchange_silent_conversion asks whether a caller can distinguish a discarded configuration change from an accepted one through the proposal result, given that raft.go:1318-1335 computes alreadyPending/alreadyJoint/wantsLeaveJoint and, when a check fails with validation enabled, replaces the proposed entry with an empty pb.Entry{Type: pb.EntryNormal}, appends it, leaves pendingConfIndex untouched, and reports no error - the remaining caller-visible signals being the library's Infof line and the unchanged ConfState, with Config.DisableConfChangeValidation (raft.go:258-278) existing to bypass exactly that conversion. The discriminator is registered rather than half-executed: on a leader in a simple configuration, propose an empty ConfChangeV2 and record the returned error, the appended entry's type and Data length at the proposed index, the ConfState before and after commit/apply, and whether a second proposal while one is pending is converted the same way, with DisableConfChangeValidation as the control that must bypass the conversion and a valid single-node conf change as the positive control. Counterevidence is recorded up front - the conversion is deliberate, explicitly logged and opt-out-able, and the applying application can see the entry type - so the question is scoped to the proposal result and to what the library, not the embedding, guarantees; no execution is requested this turn.
